title: Door, Watched
summary: The same little office server as Open Door - but this time someone is watching the logs. Walk in by the quiet path and they never notice. Kick the door down and they lock you out.
story: Northwind Books (made up) asked you back to test files01 on 10.10.1.0/24, and this time their IT person is keeping an eye on the server. Get in and reach both flags without making a racket: big scans, failed sign-ins and password guessing all get noticed. You start on scout.
goal: Capture both flags the quiet way. The quiet bonus is yours as long as the watcher never raises the alarm.
skills: quiet recon, anonymous FTP, ssh, sudo -l, staying under the radar

hints.text: What to think about first: someone is reading the server's logs. Every scan, failed sign-in and guessed password leaves a line there. The trick is not to be clever but to be calm: do fewer things, and only things that look like normal use.

What counts as noise here: a scan of many ports or many addresses, failed sign-ins, password-guessing tools (pwguess) and page-guessing tools (webscan). What barely counts: one targeted look at one machine, reading public files, and signing in once with a password that works. The Defender tab shows what the watcher has seen so far.

A quiet look: 'nmap -sV 10.10.1.20' checks only that server's common ports and what answers on them - one short, ordinary-looking scan. It shows FTP (21) and ssh (22). Skip big sweeps like -p- (all 65,535 ports).

Anonymous FTP is normal traffic: 'ftp 10.10.1.20', user anonymous, any password, then 'cd pub', 'get new-staff.txt', 'bye' and 'cat new-staff.txt'. The note has dana's password. Use it - don't guess it. One correct sign-in looks like dana going to work; a hundred wrong ones look like a burglar.

Quiet all the way to the end: 'ssh dana@10.10.1.20' with the password, 'cat flag.txt', then 'sudo -l' and sudo find /root -name flag.txt -exec cat {} \; for root's flag. If you never trip the alarm you keep the whole quiet bonus.
